description:
Teek is where a river goes to die. Having carved an improbable course into the heart of the desert, it at last spreads itself out into a wide lake and fades into the sand. It is around this strange place-of-ending that the wealthy have gathered for centuries, and it is where they now confront their own decline.

Palaces and mansions crowd about the shore: some in elegant shapes and subtle colors like the surrounding sands, others ornate with tiles of lapis and garnet. Yet others are like great glass pyramids. "Great Families" are still the nominal owners and residents of these halls, but the real power rests with the Butlers.

The title of "Butler" has long since been generalized to mean "employed" or "knowledgeable" or "cunning" - someone who holds keys and knows secrets. A Butler comes into their own when they receive their glass key from the Storm Butler, who calls lightning down upon the dunes and shapes the resultant fulgurites into ornate keys - key whose forms seem to follow patterns within Buttling families. When a Butler takes up office in a mansion, the locks are changed to fit their key.

Vastly outnumbered and in truth subservient to their servants, the Great Families carry on with their pageantry: the expensive import of goods, the acquisition of rare birds of great size, extravagant parties - but the careful observer may notice that the Families' plates seem piled less and less high as time wears on, while their appetite for "gifting" fine goods and gold to their Butlers seems to grow...
